liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (1 review, 2 other sources): Reviewer thinks Morning Dew belongs as first song of the first set, before Dark Star, not before It Hurts Me Too; This listing places Morning Dew after Good Morning Little Schoolgirl and before It Hurts Me Too [1][3][14]
- **Alligator** (2 reviews): Alligator follows the tape cut and carries through strongly to the end; Reviewer says Alligator epitomizes 1960s psychedelic rock, with standout Garcia licks between roughly the 12 and 13 minute marks [7][10]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Caution into Feedback sequence sublime; Reviewer identifies Caution, around the four-minute mark, as the song in which Phil stops playing [6][8]
- **Feedback** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds Feedback painfully harsh, likening it to a truck horn echoing in a tunnel alongside a wailing infant; Reviewer found Phil's Feedback playful and funny, not the dark, menacing wail they had expected [4][5]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this The Eleven among the greatest versions ever played [6]
- **That's It For The Other One** (1 other source): That's It For The Other One cuts off at the line about him having to die [3]

## The recordings

- **gd68-03-16.sbd.vernon.9388.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 83 min; rated 4.39/5 by 23 [1]. Said about its sound: Good soundboard sound but bass-heavy with Phil prominent; cuts occur in and out of nearly every song; Sound is very good for its age, but the tape cuts out just as Cryptical Envelopment reaches its peak; Reviewer finds the sound impeccable for such an old show, with palpable energy and excellent communication between players [6][7][10][11][14]
- **gd1968-03-16.156159.sbd.latvala.gans.eaton.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min [3]
- **gd1968-03-16.sbd.miller.109944.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 82 min; rated 3.78/5 by 9 [2]

## Around the show

- Per the book Searching for the Sound, the Phil and Jerry brawl happened after this show; Phil placed it on his 28th birthday weekend [8]
- Reviewer says the show captures the band's shift from dance-pop toward weirder territory; 2/2/68 offers more raw jamming power [5]
- Reviewer says this show was among the live recordings used in assembling the album Anthem of the Sun [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-03-16.sbd.vernon.9388.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard source; shntool confirms the tracks fall on sector boundaries [1]
- **gd1968-03-16.156159.sbd.latvala.gans.eaton.miller.flac16**: taped by Thanks to Dick Latvala, David Gans and Rob Eaton for the Dat; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 25, 2022; source: SBD > (4 Track) Master Reels > DAT (44.1k) [3]. Also: Sourced from a DAT via Dick Latvala, David Gans and Rob Eaton; over two minutes longer than the uploader's earlier source, with a reel flip between Caution and Feedback [3]
- **gd1968-03-16.sbd.miller.109944.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [2]
